title: Edmund and the Hollow
premise: Ada Yarrow, royal food-taster and secret ledger-keeper for a guild that trades in impossible things, has spent years making herself unmemorable. When a dying stranger named Edmund presses a map into her hands—a map to the door out of Vell, a country erased from every record twenty years ago—she becomes the most hunted person in the kingdom. Pursued by the Crown's inquisitors and betrayed by her own guild, Ada discovers she is heir to Vell's vanished throne, and that the 'long winter' falling over the land is the country itself trying to remember it exists. In the end, Ada chooses not to escape through the door but to hold it open, dissolving her own name into the map so that Vell—and everyone the erasure swallowed—can return, while Edmund's ghost finally rests.
about_author: Yara Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents belonging to nations that no longer exist. She writes fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the quiet violence of being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. We meet her double life: tasting the king's food by day, keeping the Hollow Guild's ledgers of impossible trades by night. She prides herself on being forgettable—no family name, no history. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Salt Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A bleeding stranger stumbles into the guild's back room, calls her by a name she's never used, and dies pressing a folded map into her hands. The guild's enforcers arrive minutes too late. Emotional beat: terror—the invisible life cracking open.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Won't Say
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She hides the map inside her ledger and discovers an entry in her own handwriting she never wrote: a debt owed to 'the door out of Vell.' The guild mistress interrogates her gently, dangerously. Emotional beat: paranoia; nothing she owns is fully hers.

chapters.title: Snow That Falls Upward
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, fleeing the capital. The first impossible snow begins falling—falling upward, unmelting. An inquisitor with a warrant made of paper that burns cold corners her in a market town; she escapes only by trading a memory of her mother. Emotional beat: grief as currency.

chapters.title: Edmund's Country
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Following the map, she reaches ruins where signs read in a language only she can suddenly parse. Edmund's ghost appears—not hostile, but tired—explaining he was Vell's last cartographer and chose her because erasure left her half outside the world. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance.

chapters.title: The Guild's Price
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Her old guild finds her and offers sanctuary—for the map. She learns the guild has been quietly selling pieces of Vell to the Crown for years, and that her immunity-building was training her body to survive the door. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only family she had.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Hale
chapters.summary: Hale's POV, first shift. The Crown's chief inquisitor hunts Ada but harbors his own erased childhood in Vell; his warrant-paper whispers to him. He catches her, then hesitates at the sight of snow falling upward on his own memories. Emotional beat: justice versus obedience.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Finishes Falling
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The winter swallows whole villages; people forget their own names mid-sentence. Ada realizes the erasure isn't punishment—it's Vell dying again, and the door is its last heartbeat. She and Hale make an uneasy pact. Emotional beat: urgency sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At the map's terminus, the guild, the Crown's soldiers, and the ghost converge. The door demands a name freely given to open from either side. Ada understands why Edmund chose her: she was born on the night of the erasure, a child of both countries. Emotional beat: acceptance of cost.

chapters.title: Ada of Vell
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She writes her true name into the ledger one final time and gives it to the door, which opens wide enough for the snow to fall downward again and the erased to step home—including Hale's remembered self. She remains, unnamed and content, keeper of a new ledger. Emotional beat: identity found by surrendering it.
